title: feat(app-shell,plugin-chatbot,i18n): launchers mark a proposed plan awaiting approval (objectui#11666)
body:
Fixes #11666
Clause-②: yes

The console chat launchers now show a marker while a proposed plan awaits the user's approval (objectui#2458 item 6). Before this, a user who closed the chat with a blueprint still waiting got no sign of it from the launcher they came back to.

## What changed

- **The reading comes from the plan card itself.** `ChatbotEnhanced` (`@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`) takes a new optional prop, `onPlanApprovalPendingChange`. It reports whether the thread's NEWEST proposed plan is still `pending` according to `resolveProposalCardState`, the one producer the card's header and body already read (objectui#7254). So the reading is true exactly when the newest plan card offers "Build it". It fires once on mount and again on every change. An approval (the optimistic "Building…" flip) or a build that ran ends it. A newer proposal supersedes the plan before it.
- **The chat pane publishes it on the assistant bus.** `ChatPane` (app-shell) publishes the reading per conversation and per signed-in user. The new bus functions are `publishPlanApprovalPending` and `usePlanApprovalPending`. They are kept off the `useAssistant` snapshot, like the bus's two event channels, so a plan's state does not re-render every snapshot consumer. Deleting a conversation from the `/ai` sidebar (`useConversationList.remove`) drops its reading.
- **Both launchers read the bus.** These are `ConsoleChatbotFab` (app pages and Home) and `ChatDockLauncher` (Studio's collapsed dock). While a reading is pending they render a small amber dot. Its text, the new key `console.ai.dock.planAwaitingApproval`, is wired as the button's accessible description through `aria-describedby`, since a button's children are presentational and a name on the dot would reach no assistive tech. With no reading pending they render nothing, and the button carries no `aria-describedby`.
- **i18n:** the key is added to all ten built-in packs.
- **Docs:** a paragraph in `packages/plugin-chatbot/README.md` documents the prop.

## Why it is built this way (measured, not assumed)

- **The chat is not mounted when a launcher shows.** `ChatDockPanel` renders only while `dock.expanded`. `ConsoleLayout` renders the FAB only while `!dock.expanded`, and Studio renders `ChatDockLauncher` only when collapsed on desktop. So no chat code is mounted to ask at the moment the marker is visible, and the reading has to outlive the chat. The bus is a module singleton that only a mounted chat writes. Every change to a plan's state in the document happens inside a mounted chat: the approval click, a newer proposal, and the build that runs.
- **What `useChatConversation` holds is a cache mirror, not the plan's state.** Its `CachedProposedPlan` is the serialization mirror for the localStorage message cache. The plan's state is derived only inside `ChatbotEnhanced`, from `builtPlanIds` and `approvedPlanIds`. Deriving it again in app-shell would have been a second producer of the same fact, which objectui#7254 ruled out. Hence the prop.
- **The spec declares no plan status.** `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0 has no `blueprint_proposed`, `awaiting_confirmation`, approved, rejected or superseded status. Its dist carries only the HITL `pending_approval` envelope. The console's declared states are `ProposalCardState` (`pending`, `in-progress`, `settled`, `failed`), and the marker keys on `pending`.
- **Keyed by conversation and owner.** Opening a chat on another thread does not clear a plan waiting in this one. Because the SPA keeps running across a sign-out (`AuthProvider` does not reload), a reading is shown only to the user it was read for.

## What it does not see (stated, not papered over)

- **A page reload** starts the bus empty. A waiting plan shows no marker until a chat on that conversation is opened again. The durable copy is the server conversation. Reading it from the launcher would need the conversation's scope (agent resolution), its messages, and the chat's plan-state derivation, which is the chat graph this card keeps out of the launcher. See Acceptance notes.
- **A decision made in another tab or on another device** is not seen until this tab's chat re-reads that thread.
- **"Reject" has no declared state.** The plan card has no reject action: "Adjust" only focuses the composer. A plan the user declines in words keeps its "Build it", and the marker mirrors the card. Keying on a guess at the user's words is what the dispatch ruled out. A rejection that leads to a newer proposal does move the marker, onto that proposal.

## Widened public surfaces (Clause-②)

1. `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot`: the exported `ChatbotEnhancedProps` type gains one optional member, `onPlanApprovalPendingChange`, a callback taking one boolean and returning nothing. The card cannot be met without it: the only producer of the plan's state is internal to `ChatbotEnhanced`.
2. `@object-ui/i18n`: one new key, `console.ai.dock.planAwaitingApproval`, in every built-in pack. The `en` pack is exported from the package entry, so the key also joins the translation-key type derived from it.

`@object-ui/app-shell` adds no export. `publishPlanApprovalPending` and `usePlanApprovalPending` ship inside `dist/` but are not on the package entry, and the exported `assistantBus` object and `AssistantSnapshot` type are unchanged. Changeset: `.changeset/11666-launcher-plan-awaiting-approval.md`, `minor` for all three packages.

## Evidence

All readings below were taken on the merged head `f678767` (the branch after one merge commit of `origin/main` at `a600924`) unless a line names another sha. Each gate's own verdict line is quoted.

- **Pins (3 new files, 33 tests).** `pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=verbose` over the three files, on `f678767`: `Test Files  3 passed (3)`, `Tests  33 passed (33)`.
  - `ChatbotEnhanced.planApprovalPending-11666.test.tsx` (plugin-chatbot) pins the producer through the real mapper (`uiMessagesToChatMessages`) and real envelopes. It covers: pending while "Build it" shows; false with no plan; false on the approve click; still true after an `awaiting_confirmation` apply (objectui#8343) and false once the build ran; following the newest plan; an older superseded plan not keeping it alive; and one announcement per change.
  - `launcherPlanApprovalMarker-11666.test.tsx` (app-shell layout) pins **both launchers in both states**: no marker and no `aria-describedby` with no reading; the marker plus accessible description `A proposed plan is waiting for your approval` with one; the zh pack's text under a zh UI; cleared when the reading turns false; not cleared by another thread's reading; and never shown for another user's reading. It also checks that every one of the ten packs names the key, and that no non-en pack copies the English text.
  - `AiChatPage.planApprovalReachesLaunchers-11666.test.tsx` (app-shell) renders the real `ChatPane` and the real FAB. It covers: the marker outliving the pane's unmount; a reopen clearing nothing until the chat reads false; another thread not clearing it; and a `/ai` sidebar delete dropping it.
- **Affected suites.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over `packages/app-shell/src/layout/`, `packages/app-shell/src/assistant/`, the wiring pin, `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/` and `packages/i18n/src/` printed `Test Files  185 passed (185)` and `Tests  2235 passed | 13 skipped (2248)`, identical on `f678767` and on the pre-merge `4828725`.
- **Type-check, lint, build.**
  - The dependency closure was built first: `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`, 29 packages, exit 0.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n type-check`, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot type-check` and `@object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0 each, on `f678767`.
  - `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell build`: exit 0, `dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (988 emitted files verified)`.
  - `lint` for app-shell, plugin-chatbot and i18n: exit 0 on `4828725`, with `0 errors` each. Per-file eslint `--format json` on the six edited source files gives identical warning counts to the base `f9f4a62`, and zero findings on the three new test files.
- **Eager-closure budget** (`node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs`, after a console `vite build`):
  - base `f9f4a62`: `Console eager closure is 3319.2 KB gzipped across 331 of 2451 chunks (budget: 3330.4 KB, headroom: 11.2 KB)`. The report's `eagerGzipBytes` is 3398847.
  - this branch before the merge, `19865e0`: 3399427 bytes, +580, over the same 331 of 2451 chunks.
  - merged head `f678767`: `Console eager closure is 3319.7 KB gzipped across 331 of 2451 chunks (budget: 3330.4 KB, headroom: 10.6 KB)`, 3399421 bytes.
  - Where the +580 sits: the `assistantBus` chunk +192, the entry `index` chunk +282, `plugin-chatbot` +96, and `i18n-locale-en` +21 (that chunk's headroom moves from 5.5 KB to 5.4 KB). No chunk joins or leaves the eager set.
- **The FAB still imports no chat code.** `ConsoleChatbotFab.tsx` imports `react`, `../assistant/assistantBus.js` and `@object-ui/i18n`. `assistantBus.ts` imports `react` and `@object-ui/auth`. In the built console, the `assistantBus` chunk's imports are `rolldown-runtime`, `vendor-react` and `infrastructure`, the chunk that carries `@object-ui/auth` and was already in the eager set at base. It has no edge to the `plugin-chatbot` chunk.
  - Measured beside it, not caused by it: `plugin-chatbot` was already an eager chunk at base (162.5 KB gzipped), reached through `ConsoleLayout`'s static `ChatDock` import and `useAiSurfaceEnabled`'s `useAgents`.
- **Ablation**, one leg per added behaviour. Run on the committed `19865e0` through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which mutates through an anchor that must hit exactly once, proves the write on disk (anchor count and blob hash), runs the pin and restores. Every leg went red in the expected direction:

  | leg | mutation | pin file | reading |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | producer | report constant `false` | producer pin | `Tests  5 failed - 2 passed (7)` |
  | publisher | `ChatPane` publishes `pending: false` | wiring pin | `Tests  4 failed (4)` |
  | FAB marker | `{planPending ? (` to `{false ? (` | launcher pin | `Tests  4 failed - 18 passed (22)` (the four FAB cases) |
  | dock-launcher marker | same, in `ChatDockLauncher` | launcher pin | `Tests  4 failed - 18 passed (22)` (the four launcher cases) |
  | owner filter | `o === owner` to `o === o` | launcher pin | `Tests  2 failed - 20 passed (22)` (both other-user cases) |
  | delete drops reading | publish line deleted | wiring pin | `Tests  1 failed - 3 passed (4)` |

  Every restore was proven by blob hash: each of the six files' on-disk hash equals its `HEAD` blob, and `git diff HEAD` was empty afterwards.
- **Repo `check:*` gates touched by the diff.** All exit 0 on `f678767`: `i18n-keys`, `i18n-drift` (`0 en value(s) changed (1 key(s) added, 0 removed`), `i18n-dead-keys` (the new key is not listed), `control-bytes`, `new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `vi-mock-specifiers`, `vi-mock-inherit`, `vi-mock-override-shape`, `test-path-roots`, `changeset-claims`, `pending-changeset-literals`, `phantom-deps`, `side-effects-array`, `unreferenced-sources` and `self-import`. `check-changeset-presence` and `check-changeset-no-major` also exit 0.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`.** Reason: it reds on packages unbuilt in this worktree (`type entry ./dist/index.d.ts is not on disk`), a prerequisite and not a judgment. It reports `0 wrong-path, 0 fabricated`, and the README edit adds prose only, no code block.
- **NOT MEASURED: live console.** Reason: the producer of `blueprint_proposed` (the build agent's `propose_blueprint`) is not in objectstack `main` (`git grep blueprint_proposed origin/main` returns nothing there), so no local stack can propose a blueprint. The unit pins are the binding reading.
- CI runs the full farm.

## Acceptance notes

Observations, not filed (no public-door measurement):

- Two unbuilt plan cards in one thread both keep a live "Build it". The older, superseded card is not made inert, the way only the latest "Open in Builder" hand-off stays actionable (objectui#2458 UX#5). Observed in the producer pin's superseded case. Carrier: none.
- `ConsoleLayout.tsx`'s import comment says the chat chunk graph (plugin-chatbot and the rest) "only downloads on first hover/click". The build reads otherwise: the `plugin-chatbot` chunk is in the eager closure at base. It is a stale comment, not touched here. Carrier: none.
- The marker's durability after a reload is the open question in the report. The candidate is a server-declared "awaiting approval" fact on the conversation, which the launcher host would read with the console's existing client.
